name: Yum! Brands, Inc.
moat_justification: Two global category leaders (KFC, Taco Bell) run as a mostly-franchised royalty toll with scale purchasing/advertising leverage, the Byte by Yum! tech platform and >60% digital mix raising franchisee switching friction, and proven pricing power with OE positive through cycles — against zero consumer switching costs and a QSR value war, franchisee-health dependence, demonstrated brand decay (Pizza Hut being sold after negative comps), GLP-1 and food-safety headline risk, and high real leverage (~$12.28B total borrowings at Q2 2026 per search results; the engine's net-debt figure misses the long-term debt series) limiting downturn flexibility.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
one_liner: Strong 7/10-moat franchisor (KFC + Taco Bell royalty toll) — but at $147.06 the weighted IRR is only 8.08% with IV@15% of $62.06, even the super-bull case (12.04%) fails to clear 15%, and the real balance sheet is levered (engine missed the long-term debt series); it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$62.06.
moat_for: KFC + Taco Bell global category leadership and brand mindshare
Mostly-franchised royalty toll — growth funded by franchisee capex, OE positive 5/5 years
Scale in purchasing, advertising funds, and development across ~64k units
Byte by Yum! platform and >60% digital mix raise franchisee switching friction
Proven pricing power — system sales still compounding ~5% ex-FX
moat_against: Zero consumer switching costs; QSR value war
Brand decay demonstrated in-portfolio — Pizza Hut sold after negative comps
Franchisee health is the real balance sheet; master-franchisee failures close units en masse
GLP-1, labor/commodity inflation, and food-safety headline risk
High leverage limits buyback flexibility in a downturn
